hook: A monochrome still image captured by a U.S. military sensor system in 2025, submitted by the FBI to AARO, showing a small dark circular object near the center of frame against an indistinct landscape background — with no accompanying mission report and an operator-confirmed inability to identify the object.
why_it_matters: This photograph represents a formal FBI submission into the AARO reporting pipeline, establishing that the bureau is actively channeling military-sourced UAP imagery to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office. The disclosure that the original imagery was redacted before submission raises questions about what was removed and by whom. The absence of a mission report leaves the operational context — altitude, platform type, time, and circumstances of capture — entirely unknown.
key_findings: The image originated from a U.S. military sensor system, not a civilian or law enforcement platform, indicating FBI is routing military UAP imagery through civilian agency channels to AARO.
The FBI redacted the original imagery before submission to AARO, meaning AARO received an already-altered version of the military sensor output.
No mission report accompanied the submission, leaving platform type, altitude, speed, and operational context undocumented in this release.
The on-image timestamp is incorrect due to the sensor system's date/time not being configured, making chronological analysis of the capture impossible from the image alone.

The object appears as a small, dark, circular form in the center-right quadrant of a grainy monochrome frame with a crosshair reticle overlay, consistent with an electro-optical or infrared targeting or surveillance sensor.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: AARO is explicitly named as the direct recipient of this FBI submission, placing this image within the formal post-2022 UAP reporting architecture.
The image derives from an unspecified U.S. military sensor system; without platform identification, a connection to Wright-Patterson's aerospace intelligence functions is plausible but unconfirmed.
